newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - December 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - December 3.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- MOVE TO IMPROVE PUBLIC'S KNOWLEDGE OF FINANCE

A new body, the Personal Finance Education Group, is to be launched this week with the aim of improving the public's understanding of pensions, life assurance and other personal financial products. The initiative is backed by the government, financial industry groups and consumer groups, and follows widespread concern after a number of scandals involving the misselling of financial products.
-- RACAL SHARES DROP 18 PERCENT ON WARNING

Shares in UK electronics group Racal fell 18 percent on Monday following a profit warning from the company. Racal cautioned investors that profits in the current financial year would be nearly a third lower than last year, prompting the 50p fall in the share price, to 225p. The warning comes despite an announcement in August that the company was on course to move operating profits "substantially ahead" and raise pre-tax profits.
-- STAGECOACH JOINS BID FOR LAST BR FREIGHT OPERATION

Transport company Stagecoach, the Scottish-based bus operator which has recently expanded into the privatised railway business, is aiming to move into freight operations with a bid for the final chunk of British Rail's freight business to be sold off. Stagecoach is joining with Freightliner, the container services operator, and with Spanish freight company Transfesa to bid for loss-making Railfreight Distribution (RfD). Bids for RfD, which operates container trains through the Channel tunnel, were submitted on Monday by the Stagecoach consortium and by US-owned company English Welsh & Scottish Railway.
-- FACTORY ORDERS BOOSTED BY STRONG DOMESTIC DEMAND

The latest monthly survey by the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply reveals that UK factory order books are improving at their fastest rate for two years, despite a weakening in factory orders from overseas caused by the stronger pound. Increased demand from domestic customers is more than compensating for that dent, with consumer goods manufacturers reporting the biggest rise in orders - pointing the way to buoyant consumer spending in the run-up to Christmas.
-- FUTURE OF 1 BILLION STG CHIP PLANT IN BALANCE

A public inquiry into plans to build a semiconductor plant on a greenfield site on the outskirts of Birmingham begins on Tuesday. The inquiry will determine the future of a possible 1 billion sterling investment by Dutch electronics group Philips in the plant. The controversial scheme has seen the Labour-dominated council side with business leaders in backing the proposals, against the objections of residents in staunchly Conservative suburbs.
-- GERMAN COMPANY RETURNS TO ROOTS

P.I.V. Antrieb Werner Reimers, a world-leading German specialist machinery drives manufacturer, is to set up a factory in the UK. The move represents a return to roots for P.I.V., as the technology on which its products are based was developed by an English inventor in the 1920s. P.I.V. says it planned the factory -- which will probably be located at the site of its sales operation in Scunthorpe -- following solid demand for its products in the UK.
-- ELECTRICITY COMPETITION TO BE PHASED IN

The planned start-date for the introduction of competition in the UK electricity supply market has been postponed, the regulator announced on Monday. The delay follows pressure from the electricity industry, which claimed that the logistical challenges of competition would require a longer period. Now, the deregulation will be phased in over six months starting April 1998, instead of commencing exactly on April 1, 1998 as previously planned.
-- SHAREHOLDERS VOTE TO OUST EMAP REBELS FROM BOARD

Media company Emap is continuing to experience boardroom unrest despite securing backing for the ousting of two dissident directors at an extraordinary general meeting. Institutional shareholders in the company are still uneasy over the question of replacements for the two directors, Professor Ken Simmonds and Joe Cooke. Emap chairman Sir John Hoskyns suggested to the meeting that the two men need not be replaced, causing confusion among the shareholders as Sir John also announced the commencement of a recruitment process for replacements for his own post and of deputy chairman Richard Winfrey, both of whom are due to retire in 18 months' time.
-- SAGA PETROLEUM WINS AUCTION OF KUWAITI OIL GROUP

Norwegian independent oil explorer Saga Petroleum has won the auction to acquire the Kuwaiti-owned North Sea oil company Santa Fe Exploration. Saga beat rival bids from Conoco, Chevron and Arco to secure the deal with an offer of $1.23 billion. The acquisition is expected to be financed by Saga via retained earnings and existing borrowing facilities. Advisors to the company believe a rights issue will not be necessary.
-- 'JOBS CUT' IN LUCASVARITY SHAKE-UP

LucasVarity, the Anglo-American automotive and aerospace components group formed via a 3.2 billion stg merger earlier this year, is expected to announce Tuesday a fundamental restructuring of its manufacturing operations. The move to accelerate LucasVarity's 115 million stg cost savings programme could lead to the closure of some plants to avoid duplication, entailing the loss of several thousand jobs. The group is also expected to reveal its disposal candidates, with Varity's brakes and wheels subsidiary Dayton Walther a strong contender for the list.
